note: THE CASE THAT PROVES THE TWO EVENTS ARE TWO COLUMNS. Seven hand-built bars, every number derivable on paper. Bars 0-4 are a clean uptrend: SAR seeds at bars[0].l = 98 and climbs 98 / 98 / 98.36 / 98.9712 while the close stays above it. Bar 5 is an OUTSIDE REVERSAL: its low (95) takes out the projected SAR (99.87408) so the trend flips DOWN and the SAR jumps to the prior extreme point (ep = 108) — but its close (112) is ABOVE that, so the price did NOT change sides. trendFlipped=1, priceCrossedSar=0. Bar 6 is the mirror: the downtrend clamps SAR up to the prior high (113), the close (107) is now below it, and the side changes with no trend change. trendFlipped=0, priceCrossedSar=1. On `sar_default`'s 140 real bars the two columns are element-for-element EQUAL, so without this case a lane that returned the same column twice — or returned them the wrong way round — would be invisible.
